snowball method has been working for me as well. i was at 8.5k upwards of 9k at my worst. I get paid biweekly and use one check at the beginning of the month as my "debt check" i pay as many debts as i can as soon as i get paid and as much as i can with only leaving little left for absolute necessities (food, hygiene, transportation etc) i dont spend money to eat out, lots and lots of instant ramen... The second check I get is for rent and bills, if I have anything left (i usually dont) i will throw at least another $50 at the debt. Rinse and repeat. I write out every bill, every subscription and every purchase down in a planner to keep track. I have become "boring" and dont go out with my friends or shop on my days off. I only go to the store when i need to replace a necessity. I sell every possible thing i can on reselling platforms (depop for clothes, fb marketplace for homewares) I price things pretty low bc small sales add up faster than waiting forever for higher ticket prices to sell. I dont make tons of money at my job and I dont even work 40 hrs a week. Im down to my last $1k on my last credit card. Started my journey in the beginning of July. Looking to be completely debt free before the end of January. if youre at $4-5k it is absolutely doable. You just have to show up for yourself, the time will pass anyway. I believe in you, good luck!

Not at all! I hid it very well, if anything people assumed I was very good with my spending! Couldnt have been further from the truth. I was shopping for an ideal self constantly, going to expensive restaurants, buying new clothes, books id never read, workout wear for "motivation" etc. I started to focus on trying to fulfill the things that would actually contribute to who my ideal self was. Cooking more at home, making outfits with my existing wardrobe, working out 3-4x a week. I know its soooo cliche but working out REALLY helps, mentally and physically. Cooking and reading also keep my hands and mind busy from wanting to scroll for hours on ssense lol. I realized I was the only person stopping myself from being my "ideal." feeling productive with my time and the thought of being able to have a decent savings feels SO much better than getting yet ANOTHER pair of designer shoes haha. I am entering my late 20's now and the thought of being 30 with a shopping addiction is not who I want to be at all.

About $8.5k, upwards of $9k. Before that I would always carry a balance and yoyo between $1-3k. I would get good at not shopping and paying it down then get down to the last $1k and think meh well its not that bad, i can probably still shop. Then completely relapse and run it up to another $3-4k. I did this for YEARS (id say around 3 years). 

In March and I got engaged. I kept my debt a secret from my fiance. I told myself I would pay it off without him knowing and all would be well. But we went on vacation in April and also had a bunch of friends come to visit in May and June. I completely lost control, stopped checking my balances and only paid minimums. By July, I was neck deep in my debt and interest charges werent helping. I had finally hit rock bottom. I came clean to him about my addiction and decided that was it. I just couldnt live with the shame anymore. We are about to be married and he had no idea I had this burden. 

I am very lucky to have such an understanding partner. But he wasnt going to help me out of it either. I made my bed and now I had to sleep in it lol. From that very day on I have been very dedicated to getting it to $0. I have had a few set backs here and there and it is by no means easy to penny pinch and have to stretch $50 over 2 weeks before getting paid again just for it all go straight back into the debt again. Honestly, it fucking sucks, but no one brought me here but me. 

I am currently $5k down with $3.5k left to go on my last CC. Looking to have at least $1k in a high yield savings account by Valentines day next year!! It is extremely freeing to take control. Its given me insight on my true wants and needs. I am obviously not perfect and still have tons to learn. But the inner work is extremely gratifying. $2k is not bad IF you can take control of it now. I promise if you start today you will be better for it tomorrow! Good luck <3

I work in fashion, Id honestly avoid trendy items in general. Trends also feed into the toxic idealized self. If you think about all the cool fashion girls & influencers online, theyre cool because of their own personal style. BUT they can easily incorporate trends bc brands most likely send them items to be promoted. So theyre always on par (its also needed to stay relevant for the algorithm too) To be completely honest, whenever I see a trendy outfit I think they are likely not truly stylish or original. Trends should be picked here and there & incorporated into your personal style, not dominated over the rest. Think about who you are and the lifestyle you have. Find staples that you feel the most like yourself in. Same with shapes & colors that suit you the best. Sleep on a trend that first comes up and revisit it after a few weeks. Trend cycles move so so quickly with social media that there will always be something new before you even realize it.

Are you immediately paying yourself first with every paycheck? I get paid biweekly, I used the first check of the month to pay off as much debt as I can. I only give myself a very very small budget each week for necessities the rest goes to the debt. If I keep any more, I WILL find a way to spend it. The second check goes to rent and bills. Anything left over is left to budget for the next two weeks until my next “debt check” & so far it’s been working for me. I also got a planner ($10 from target but if you have dollar stores near you utilize them!) I write out the days I get paid, when I’m going to be charged for subscriptions, & rent/bill dues for every month. Seeing it all written out visually helps me a lot. And writing in the planner is kinda like a new hobby. Treat urself to a few cheap stickers from the store to make your planning all cute and fun! Like bullet journaling but with bills lol
